newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds firm but below pre-holiday peaks.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds firm but below pre-holiday peaks.

text.p: *Australian bonds returned from Monday's holiday firm, although prices were below the peaks seen just before the long weekend as U.S. Treasuries pared Friday's strong advance.
*ANZ jobs ads series for May due at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
Australian bonds returned from the long weekend firm, although prices were below the peaks seen just before the break as U.S. Treasuries pared Friday's strong advance on Monday.
The June 10-year bond futures contract raced to a six month high of 92.830 during Friday's after hours session, which had taken the equivalent benchmark 10-year bond below 7.25 percent.

The move followed a steep rally in U.S. Treasuries which jumped on data showing a moderation in job creation in Friday's May U.S. non-farm payrolls rather than the fall in unemployment to a near 24-year low.
However, the U.S. market subsequently gave up some ground during Monday's session.

"I think local gains will be a struggle from here unless we get something out of this week's data with the 10-year yield now around 7.25 percent and the three-year just 60 basis points over cash," one trader said.
This Thursday's labour force data for May will be keenly watched and a weak outcome could fuel talk of a further easing in monetary policy.
A prelude to the report will the ANZ job advertisements series for May at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT).
The local market showed a narrowing bias to the dollar bloc, although it was outpaced by the long end of the Canadian curve.
The yield curve flattened slightly as the long-end benefitted more from the net advance in U.S. Treasuries either side of the weekend.
